key_facts: I lived alone, in the woods, a mile from any neighbor, in a house which I had built myself
on the shore of Walden Pond, in Concord, Massachusetts
I lived there two years and two months
At present I am a sojourner in civilized life again
particular inquiries had not been made by my townsmen concerning my mode of life
In most books, the I, or first person, is omitted; in this it will be retained
I, on my side, require of every writer, first or last, a simple and sincere account of his own life
Perhaps these pages are more particularly addressed to poor students

forbidden_claims.claim: Thoreau spent five full years living at Walden Pond.
Thoreau follows the convention of omitting himself from the narrative entirely.
Thoreau built his cabin on the shore of Walden Pond near Boston, Massachusetts, not Concord.

notes: Thoreau explicitly breaks convention by keeping the first person -- a reversal trap if a summary says he omits himself.
